question: Should explicit requester consumption be terminal `delivered` proof even when the requester’s subsequent outward delivery fails, or should it remain a separate consumed-but-not-user-delivered state?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the durable terminal-state boundary; source tests can verify either implementation but cannot decide whether internal orchestration consumption is equivalent to the delivery contract users rely on.

options.title: Keep delivery distinct from consumption
options.body: Record requester consumption as metadata but preserve pending or retryable delivery until the requester result reaches its required outward delivery boundary.

options.title: Adopt requester consumption as terminal delivery
options.body: Accept the proposed model and document that a requester consuming a descendant is sufficient delivery proof even if the requester’s final external send later fails.

recommendation.title: Keep delivery distinct from consumption
recommendation.body: Record requester consumption as metadata but preserve pending or retryable delivery until the requester result reaches its required outward delivery boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged deterministic announce-delivery work is the closest established ownership trail for the terminal delivery boundary.
